commit_message:
avformat/mov: don't assume iloc and iinf entries for each item_id will be in the same order

Nothing forbids them to be in any order the muxer desires.

Fixes demuxing heif samples generated by S1II.

Tested-by: Lynne <dev@lynne.ee>
Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>

fix_commit_message:
avformat/mov: abort if the queried item doesn't exist instead of overwriting it

The check for item presence was insufficient as it would result in the last
item in the array being overwritten if it existed even if the id didn't match.

Fixes: Assertion ref failed at src/libavformat/mov.c:10649
Fixes: clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_dem_MOV_fuzzer-5312542695292928
Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg

Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: The fix commit adds a post-loop check (`if (j == c->nb_heif_item) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;` / `if (i == c->nb_heif_item) ...`) in both mov_read_iloc() and mov_read_infe() to detect the case where the search-or-allocate loop over c->heif_item[] completes without finding a matching item_id or allocating a new slot, which previously led to overwriting an unrelated item. I replicated this exact logic on top of the intro commit's code: converted the loop variables (j in iloc, i in infe) to be declared outside the for-loop so they remain in scope after the loop, and added the termination check right after the existing `if (!item) return AVERROR(ENOMEM);` checks, without altering any other unrelated logic (I initially over-applied unrelated hunks from a later diff context and then corrected that back to match the actual on-disk code structure).
